    Fees, deposit and why TBLOCK

    Before your wallet opens, review your name, symbol, engraved face and brain, selected pair, and the price: $5 in all, TBLOCK first. Step 1, only if you lack TBLOCK: the app buys it with your ETH (no app fee). Step 2, the birth: 0.001 ETH (inside the total above), signed in two parts: 0.0007 ETH when you create, then 0.0003 ETH plus your creator deposit (not a fee: it stays yours) when its market opens. Step 3: your block is paid in TBLOCK to the holders vault. Your wallet shows the exact transaction(s) before you approve; nothing is sent until you confirm.

    Recommended: hold TBLOCK, the app's own token. About $5 of it can be bought in the app in one batch (Buy TBLOCK); $15 opens the holders' channel. Each buy goes through its pool, whose hook sends part of every trade to the dead address. Once your block is alive, you can add the rest up to $5 in TBLOCK to the holders vault (optional, one more signature). Creators can also enter their block in the block contest, where entries and votes are paid in TBLOCK.

            Borrow against several stocks at once

            Each stock is its own Morpho position: if one stock falls to its liquidation price, only that position is liquidated — the other stocks do not protect it.

              No USDC yet? Add USDC with a card or bank (Coinbase — needs a Coinbase account outside the U.S.) — it lands in your wallet, then lend it here.

              Risks: interest grows while a loan is open; if the stock falls to the liquidation price, your collateral is sold to repay the debt. When stock markets are closed, the oracle price can stay still. Lending markets are Morpho’s, not ours.

              Brain AI

              128 spiking neurons per block, seeded by its address. Not an LLM — feeds on market + chain, moves the block, signs nothing. Option A: it proposes; you pay; it writes the journal — never freestyle-signs markets. Pick any listed block — TBLOCK is not forced.

              — 0 ticks

              Each column is one beat, each dot a neuron that fired.

              ≋ — Hz left ≋ — Hz right ⤳ — steering ⚡ — spikes since open ◉ — firing now 🧠 — memory

              What these numbers mean
              • Hz left / right — how fast each wing beats. Each wing listens to a different third of the neurons.
              • Steering — left minus right, from −1 to 1. Negative turns left, positive turns right. It is what moves the block on the map.
              • Spikes since open — every neuron firing counted since you opened this block here.
              • Firing now — neurons that fired on this beat, out of 128. More than 8 makes it curious.
              • Memory — each neuron keeps a trace of what it just did, and that trace primes it on the next beats. It fades in about thirty beats, it is kept in this browser, and the brain resumes where it was when you come back.
              • Its food — its market, plus what the chain shows in the recent window: transfers, holders reached and messages. The creation itself does not count.
              • Death — only when its creator held it and now holds none. A creator who never held it, or a balance we could not read, never kills a block.

              Food not read yet.

                    Its rules — code it writes itself
      
                    After it has seen the same event on chain at least twice, it writes a rule for it. A closed engine
        reads these lines: a rule can only write in its journal or suggest a gesture to you. It never signs, sends or
        reads anything by itself.
                    
      
                    
      
                    
      
                    
      
      
                    Its memory, written on chain
      
                    
        
        
      
                    
      
                    One signature: a transfer of 0 of this block to yourself, whose memo carries this beat, its fingerprint and its 128 neurons (rounded, ±0.27). Nothing moves; you pay the gas.
                    
      
                    
      
                    Exact copy, in 4 fragments
      
                    4 signatures of 32 neurons each (a memo holds 256 bytes) — the brain exactly as it is now, not a smarter one.

                      Tokenize something
                      
      
      
                      Create a new block on Base that carries the name of something that already exists. The original stays where it is: nothing is moved, wrapped or converted. Nothing on this screen asks you to sign.
                      
      
                      
        
        
      
                      

      
      
                      
        
        
                      Paste any ERC-20 on Base. We read its name and symbol from the chain and fill them into Create — you then mint a separate block with that name. The token itself is left untouched, and your block is not paired with it: a block opens its market against ETH, USDC, cbBTC, a tokenized stock, or another block.
                      
        
        
                      Nothing is signed here — this only reads the token and fills in the Create form.
                      
        
        
                      What this does, and what it does not
        
                        
          
                      • It makes a new block that carries that token's name and symbol — it does not move, wrap or lock the token itself.
                        • 
          
                      • Nothing backs it. No one redeems it, and its price can drift from the token from the first trade onward.
                        • 
          
          
                      • The supply is 1 billion, minted to you at birth. You do not choose it — so one block stands for however much of the source token that billion covers, and the screen shows that ratio before you sign. The cap is set to that billion, and your wallet becomes the block's admin: only an admin can raise the cap later.
                        • 
          
                      • Symbols of issued stocks are refused — a block named like a real tokenized stock would back nothing.
                        • 
          
          
          
                      • Cost: the same 0.001 ETH Birth fee as any block, when you sign in Create. Trading it then costs what its market charges — 3% on a market opened here; the market screen shows the exact rate of the pool you trade in.
                        •

                        2.

                        4.

On the block's page, we later show what X returns for that link.

                      Why some cubes are bigger
      
                      
      
                      
        
                      Big cubeIts market is worth more: price × number of tokens, read from the chain.
                      
        
                      Small cubeA small market — around $1,000 or less.
                      
        
                      Pale cubeNo market yet: nobody can buy it for now.
                      
        
                      ⚠️ CarefulPrices move fast, and a small purchase can make a cube grow a lot.
          A big cube is not a big pile of money.

        How it works
        
        
                                                                          Your ticket is a block face made from your wallet and the day — one per wallet per day.
                                                                          
        
                                                                          
          
                                                                          01 · THE TICKET
                                                                          Reach $10 in a day (UTC) — trades of UNIT or tokenized stocks, paid rolls and the Week pass all count — or mint a skin, and that day's ticket is yours.
                                                                          
          
                                                                          02 · THE WEEK'S POT
                                                                          Today's ticket = 1 entry in this week's reward pot; the pot is shared by entries after the week closes (UTC). A Week pass adds 3 entries, a brain at level 3 or 6 adds 1 or 2. Each share is signed by the verifier wallet, and you claim yours from your wallet.
                                                                          
          
                                                                          03 · ROLLS
                                                                          Roll: each roll draws a new random face for you; the block after next draws its face; traits in common, out of 5. With a wallet, a roll is paid in USDC and a winning score pays from the roll pot the prize set by the current rules (read live); the UNIT creator can change them for later rolls — never more than the pot holds, and the pot can be empty. Without a wallet the roll is practice: no prize.
                                                                          
          
                                                                          04 · MISSIONS
                                                                          Anyone posts a task and locks its reward. A ticket holder who holds the block does it — a person or an AI agent — and the chain proves it. Doer 90%, community earn pool 7%, TokenizedBlock 3%.
                                                                          
          
                                                                          05 · SKINS
                                                                          Mint a skin for your block, wear it, resell it at a fixed price or in an auction (bids +5%, 7 days max). A minted skin is also that day's ticket.
                                                                          
          
          
                                                                          06 · DUELS
                                                                          Two wallets — a person, or a block's brain proposing to its owner — stake the same in USDC or an admitted tokenized stock. Each plays a new random block face; the block 2 blocks after the join draws its face; the most traits in common out of 5 wins 90% of the pot, 7% goes to the community reward pool, 3% to TokenizedBlock. A tie refunds both, no fee. Not accepted in time, or not settled within 256 blocks: refunded in full. Opens with its contract.

                                                                          How to read this view
                                                                          
    
                                                                            
      
                                                                          • Inside: you are among its neurons. Lit = fired on this beat; faint = its 5 beats before. Warm from the front = a buy reached it, cold from behind = a sell, shimmer at the sides = a transfer, a new speck = a new holder. Its inputs sit on an arc in front of it (their real value, or "not read"); labels show for what you point at and the nearest few.
                                                                            • 
      
                                                                          • Outside: its real neighbours on the map, by their world positions. They stay dim: its neurons read none of them.
                                                                            • 
      
                                                                          • The light is its mood; the edge pulse, how many neurons fired; the horizon tilts with its steering. The beat number at the top is the beat on screen, and the overlay speaks of that same beat.
                                                                            • 
      
                                                                          • Take control: a LOCAL snapshot of the beat on screen ("Snapshot of beat N") — drag to orbit its 128 neurons, inputs and neighbours, scroll to fly, right-drag or Shift-drag to move. Nothing is sent, nothing is signed.
                                                                            • 
      
                                                                          • The centre ring shows what the camera looks at; click an object to pin its overlay, click empty space to release.
                                                                            • 
    
                                                                          
  
                                                                          Inspect — everything this page holds about it: each line is read (with its source), not read, or has no source in this app
